title: Customer account lifecycle through the partner Account API, with shop sign-in

sourcesRead.contributes: description, team notes (test data, login page, out of scope), AC-1..AC-12
base URL, encoding, response envelope (responseCode vs HTTP 200), endpoints, required fields, exact messages

actors: customer signing in to the shop
context: The partner manages Automation Exercise customer accounts through the Account API (create, check credentials, read, update, close). Partner-created customers must be able to sign in to the shop with the same e-mail and password; closed accounts must not. The attached account-api-contract.md (v1.2, status agreed) is the reference for parameter names, required fields, response codes and messages.

acceptanceCriteria.quote: The system shall create a customer account when the partner calls createAccount with all required fields and an e-mail address not yet registered, answering responseCode 201 with the message "User created!".
acceptanceCriteria.text: The system shall create a customer account when the partner calls createAccount with all required fields and an e-mail address not yet registered, answering responseCode 201 with the message "User created!".
outcomes: createAccount with all required fields and a new e-mail -> responseCode 201
message "User created!"

acceptanceCriteria.quote: The system shall refuse to create a second account for an e-mail address that is already registered, answering responseCode 400 with the message "Email already exists!".
acceptanceCriteria.text: The system shall refuse to create a second account for an e-mail address that is already registered, answering responseCode 400 with the message "Email already exists!".
outcomes: createAccount with an already registered e-mail -> responseCode 400
message "Email already exists!"

acceptanceCriteria.quote: The system shall treat e-mail addresses case-insensitively for uniqueness: registering an address that differs from an existing account's address only in letter case shall be refused exactly as in AC-2.
acceptanceCriteria.text: The system shall treat e-mail addresses case-insensitively for uniqueness: registering an address that differs from an existing account's address only in letter case shall be refused exactly as in AC-2.
outcomes: createAccount with an existing account's e-mail differing only in letter case -> responseCode 400
message "Email already exists!"

acceptanceCriteria.quote: The system shall refuse createAccount when any required field of the contract is missing, answering responseCode 400 with the message naming the missing parameter, and shall not create the account.
acceptanceCriteria.text: The system shall refuse createAccount when any required field of the contract is missing, answering responseCode 400 with the message naming the missing parameter, and shall not create the account.
outcomes: createAccount without one required field (name, email, password, firstname, lastname, address1, country, zipcode, state, city, mobile_number) -> responseCode 400
message "Bad request, <field> parameter is missing in POST request." naming the missing field (e.g. "Bad request, city parameter is missing in POST request.")
the account is not created: getUserDetailByEmail for that e-mail gives responseCode 404 "Account not found with this email, try another email!"

acceptanceCriteria.quote: The system shall refuse createAccount when the e-mail address is not a valid e-mail address (for example it has no "@"), answering responseCode 400, and shall not create the account.
acceptanceCriteria.text: The system shall refuse createAccount when the e-mail address is not a valid e-mail address (for example it has no "@"), answering responseCode 400, and shall not create the account.
outcomes: createAccount with an e-mail that has no @ -> responseCode 400 (message not fixed by the contract)
the account is not created: getUserDetailByEmail for that address gives responseCode 404

acceptanceCriteria.quote: The system shall answer verifyLogin as the contract states: valid e-mail and password give responseCode 200 "User exists!"; a wrong password or an unknown e-mail give responseCode 404 "User not found!"; a missing e-mail or password gives responseCode 400 "Bad request, email or password parameter is missing in POST request."; the DELETE method gives responseCode 405 "This request method is not supported.".
acceptanceCriteria.text: The system shall answer verifyLogin as the contract states: valid e-mail and password give responseCode 200 "User exists!"; a wrong password or an unknown e-mail give responseCode 404 "User not found!"; a missing e-mail or password gives responseCode 400 "Bad request, email or password parameter is missing in POST request."; the DELETE method gives responseCode 405 "This request method is not supported.".
outcomes: valid e-mail and password -> responseCode 200 "User exists!"
wrong password -> responseCode 404 "User not found!"
unknown e-mail -> responseCode 404 "User not found!"
e-mail missing -> responseCode 400 "Bad request, email or password parameter is missing in POST request."
password missing -> responseCode 400 "Bad request, email or password parameter is missing in POST request."
DELETE method on verifyLogin -> responseCode 405 "This request method is not supported."

acceptanceCriteria.quote: The system shall return the customer's profile from getUserDetailByEmail with every field listed in the contract, holding the values given at registration, and shall never return the password; an unknown e-mail gives responseCode 404 "Account not found with this email, try another email!".
acceptanceCriteria.text: The system shall return the customer's profile from getUserDetailByEmail with every field listed in the contract, holding the values given at registration, and shall never return the password; an unknown e-mail gives responseCode 404 "Account not found with this email, try another email!".
outcomes: known e-mail -> responseCode 200 with a user object
the user object has every field: id, name, email, title, birth_day, birth_month, birth_year, first_name, last_name, company, address1, address2, country, state, city, zipcode, mobile_number
each field holds the value given at registration (request-to-response name mapping per G3)
the password is never returned
unknown e-mail -> responseCode 404 "Account not found with this email, try another email!"

acceptanceCriteria.quote: The system shall apply updateAccount as a partial update: with the correct e-mail and password, only the fields sent change (responseCode 200 "User updated!") and the change is visible through getUserDetailByEmail; with a wrong password the answer is responseCode 404 "Account not found!" and nothing changes.
acceptanceCriteria.text: The system shall apply updateAccount as a partial update: with the correct e-mail and password, only the fields sent change (responseCode 200 "User updated!") and the change is visible through getUserDetailByEmail; with a wrong password the answer is responseCode 404 "Account not found!" and nothing changes.
outcomes: updateAccount with correct e-mail and password and some fields -> responseCode 200 "User updated!"
getUserDetailByEmail shows the sent fields changed and every field not sent unchanged
updateAccount with a wrong password -> responseCode 404 "Account not found!"
after the wrong-password update getUserDetailByEmail shows nothing changed

acceptanceCriteria.quote: The system shall close the account on deleteAccount with the correct e-mail and password (responseCode 200 "Account deleted!"), after which verifyLogin and getUserDetailByEmail answer 404 for that e-mail; with a wrong password the answer is responseCode 404 "Account not found!" and the account remains usable.
acceptanceCriteria.text: The system shall close the account on deleteAccount with the correct e-mail and password (responseCode 200 "Account deleted!"), after which verifyLogin and getUserDetailByEmail answer 404 for that e-mail; with a wrong password the answer is responseCode 404 "Account not found!" and the account remains usable.
outcomes: deleteAccount with correct e-mail and password -> responseCode 200 "Account deleted!"
afterwards verifyLogin for that e-mail -> responseCode 404 "User not found!"
afterwards getUserDetailByEmail for that e-mail -> responseCode 404 "Account not found with this email, try another email!"
deleteAccount with a wrong password -> responseCode 404 "Account not found!"
after the wrong-password delete the account remains usable (reading per G4: verifyLogin with the correct password -> responseCode 200 "User exists!" and getUserDetailByEmail -> responseCode 200)

endpoints.request: application/x-www-form-urlencoded form fields in the request body (attachment L10, example L106-L114). Required: name, email, password, firstname, lastname, address1, country, zipcode, state, city, mobile_number.
form fields email, password (both required) in the request body

endpoints.success: not supported: responseCode 405 "This request method is not supported."
endpoints.request: DELETE on verifyLogin (unsupported method case of AC-6)

endpoints.success: HTTP 200, body responseCode 200 and a user object
endpoints.request: query-string parameter email (?email=<email>); GET is the only method that uses the query string (attachment L10)
form fields in the request body: email and password (required, identify and authorise) plus any registration fields to change
form fields email, password in the request body (not the query string)

auth.mechanism: None at transport level. Account operations are authorised by the customer's email + password pair sent with the request.

rules.text: Every response of the Account API endpoints is delivered with HTTP status 200; the business outcome is carried in the JSON body as responseCode (integer) and message (string). All codes in the contract, and in the acceptance criteria, refer to responseCode, never to the HTTP status.
Messages in the contract are exact.

createAccount required fields: name, email, password, firstname, lastname, address1, country, zipcode, state, city, mobile_number. Optional: title (Mr, Mrs or Miss), birth_date, birth_month, birth_year, company, address2.
email must be a valid e-mail address and is unique across customers, compared case-insensitively.
name is the display name shown in the shop header after sign-in.

getUserDetailByEmail returns a user object with id, name, email, title, birth_day, birth_month, birth_year, first_name, last_name, company, address1, address2, country, state, city, zipcode, mobile_number; the password is never returned.
updateAccount is a partial update: email and password identify and authorise the customer; fields not sent keep their value.
Customers created by the partner can sign in to the shop straight away with the same e-mail and password; a closed account can no longer sign in.

testData.strategy: Tests create their own customers through the API (POST /api/createAccount); there is no pre-provisioned account.
constraints: use a fresh, unique e-mail address for every customer
the password for customers created for acceptance comes from the environment variable AE_USER_PASSWORD; never hard-code it
testData.cleanup: close (delete) every customer created, through DELETE /api/deleteAccount
